title: How Many Tons Before the Bridge Breaks? 🌉
description:
Comment A, B, C or D 👇 How many tons before this bridge breaks? Pick before the load starts to climb!

A truss bridge is built from springs, and a stack of weights grows on its deck, 5 tons per slab. Every beam is colored by how close it is to its own snap limit, cool teal to hot red. Beam sizes are the rules, drawn on screen: a dotted fuse beam snaps at 0.35% stretch or squeeze, a thin beam at 1.2%, a medium beam at 3% and a thick beam at 4.5%. A beam past 100% of its limit snaps, and the rest take its load and the deck sags. The load is added slowly, so every state is solved at rest. The bridge counts as fallen when the weight has sunk by 40% of the truss height or the roller end has slid in, and then it drops. The load counter races at the start and slows near the end, but it always shows the real tons. A band is crossed out the moment the load passes its top edge: A under 45 tons, B 45 to 59, C 60 to 74, D 75 and up. The band that holds the collapse wins. It is a simplified spring model, not engineering advice.
Everything here is generated by code (seed 587), with no footage, samples or stock media.
Which band did you pick?
